findings_assessed.finding_text: FKTP ICD-10 error rate ~55% (range 33-73%) drives BPJS claim friction
counter_evidence: Pramono 2021 systematic review shows 26-45% accurate range (19 pp spread) -- may be skewed
Publication bias: voluntary single-facility audits oversample poor performers; no national random-sample audit exists
Puskesmas Kijang study shows 33.3% error -- at lower bound
True system median may cluster closer to 33% than 55%
findings_assessed.reasoning: 55% is directionally correct but publication bias means true average may be lower. Add caveat noting selection effect; AI ROI case holds at 33% error but cost model changes.

findings_assessed.finding_text: PMCare 1.3% outpatient denial rate (revised down from 67% specialist GL revocation)
counter_evidence: CodeBlue Oct 2025: 99% of 855 specialists perceive TPA interference, 73% report patients forced to public hospitals
1.3% self-disclosed by PMCare under political pressure; not BNM audited
1.3% excludes pre-auth deferrals, partial payments, 10-15% panel fee deductions, 2-3 month payment delays
GP friction is delay + deduction, not denial -- the 1.3% creates a false impression that TPA friction is minor
findings_assessed.reasoning: 1.3% is real but covers only formal denials; add caveat that formal denial rate and total economic friction rate are different metrics.

findings_assessed.finding_text: Malaysia is the faster path to pilot vs Indonesia
counter_evidence: HealthTechAsia (Jan 2026): 91% of Indonesia primary care facilities and 95% hospitals SATUSEHAT-integrated
GovInsider (2025): 99% of 10,000+ puskesmas have digital recording via SATUSEHAT
The 8.9% FKTP EMR figure is SINGLE-VENDOR (Medeva/PT MTK) PRIVATE klinik pratama market share, not SATUSEHAT national integration
If SATUSEHAT integration is operationally substantive, Indonesia EHR data infrastructure rivals or exceeds Malaysia for a PROLANIS-channel pilot
findings_assessed.reasoning: Highest priority gap. The Malaysia-faster verdict's most empirically specific pillar is Indonesia's claimed EMR weakness. SATUSEHAT 91%/99% figures need verification + assessment of operational depth + PCare API access. Could reverse or rebalance the EHR layer of the readiness matrix.

findings_assessed.finding_text: PROLANIS recall failure as systemic CDM leakage
counter_evidence: PMC 2021 SAGE: PROLANIS effective on HbA1c/BMI/lipids when patients attend -- clinical effectiveness is real
Public Health of Indonesia 2024: 53.3% target achievement initially, declining to 40% at 18 months (decay curve, not pure structural failure)
PMC 2025 scoping review identifies 5 barrier categories; socioeconomic/cost and cultural/literacy barriers (2 of 5) are NOT addressable by AI recall automation
findings_assessed.reasoning: PROLANIS leakage is real. But AI recall automation may address only 40-60% of total leakage; the rest is socioeconomic/cultural and not technical.

summary.highest_priority_gap: F3 — SATUSEHAT 91% PC integration potentially reverses the EHR-data-infrastructure pillar of the Malaysia-faster verdict
summary.key_definitional_risk: Corpus conflates two different Indonesia EMR metrics: (1) 8.9% single-vendor private klinik pratama market share; (2) SATUSEHAT national integration rate across all PC types incl puskesmas (reported 91%)
